topics.title: Noble's walk-through

Each question has a recommended default, so the dispatches build on it unless you object. Read the topic reports alongside: each question cites its NW ids.

questions.q: Where do the six tags outside Noble's four groups go?
questions.context:
What this is about. No outdoor space, 6+ months, Full service, Renovated, Water views and New development fit none of Noble's groups (NW-045).

Why it needs you. The server rejects a tag no longer on the list, so renaming or dropping one needs a data migration. Keeping every current string avoids it.
options: Similarities for Full service, Renovated, Water views, New development; a "Differences" group for No outdoor space and 6+ months
Drop the ones a feature or check already says
needs a migration of stored tags

questions.q: Should the five-row price table also go in the email?
questions.context:
What this is about. The price table on Findings runs 10 to 12 rows and confused Noble. The replacement is five rows (low, three inner points, high) plus a calculator (NW-065).

Why it needs you. The email uses the same rows today (Frankie's full steps). One table everywhere is easier to explain, and the writer and QA then check what the agent saw.
options: Five rows on Findings and in the email
Five on Findings, the full steps in the email
Five everywhere, full steps behind a "more rows" link on Findings

questions.q: Should Hubert see the agent's own number and the target after the reveal?
questions.short: Hubert sees the target and your call
questions.context:
What this is about. D-4 said Hubert sees the target once the result is shown. The build never shows it (NW-068, NW-093). The fix is a new prompt version. The numbers are computed without the target either way, and the writer stays blind.

Why it needs you. D-4 covers only the target. The agent sees their own Gate number beside the estimate, and Hubert could use it to explain the gap.
options: read-only; never in the email or the writer

questions.q: Which good email is the example, and who writes it?
questions.context:
What this is about. Noble wants a good email agents can look at (NW-085). It later serves Sort notes and headlines too.

Why it needs you. It sets the bar for Casa's voice. The Barclay sample uses the engine's own numbers; Noble approves the voice. It needs the writer's real eval run, which waits on TD-3's key.
options: The 100 Barclay sample, drafted by the writer, edited by Noble
You write one by hand against the sample's numbers

questions.q: May an agent mark a report as sent without using the Copy button?
questions.context:
What this is about. Noble could not reach Done (NW-086). Mark as sent only turns on after a copy through the button. A hand copy from the textarea never does.

Why it needs you. Allowing it changes a rule you set. The copy log would still record only real copies.
options: Yes, Mark as sent always works
No, a button copy comes first

questions.q: Does the writer move to Collister, the new AI track?
questions.context:
What this is about. You defined Collister as owner of all AI prompts, tools and context (NW-093 a). It takes Hubert. The writer (Dispatch 13 phase 2) is also a Claude call with a prompt and an eval.

Why it needs you. Splitting AI work across two tracks recreates the problem Collister is for. Mason keeps Send UI, QA and fair-housing. Collister starts after the account move.
options: Yes, Collister owns the writer's prompts and eval
No, the writer stays with Mason

questions.q: Should deal terms (seller target, price, rate, down payment) reach Hubert after the reveal?
questions.context:
What this is about. They are kept out today as a seller's target is a deal term (NW-068).

Why it needs you. Decide with the client fields (NW-074) so privacy and the fair-housing limits are set once.
options: Include them after the reveal, same rule as the target

questions.q: Who may start and reset a sample report?
questions.context:
What this is about. Noble and Kara review flows and can't use the sample today (NW-054). A co-op sample is added.

Why it needs you. Replies and Hubert's transcript can't be deleted, so a truly clean reset means a new report from the same code and the old one archived (new link).

Until you answer, the server keeps samples admin-only. A widens it to mentors (Dispatch 23 items 1–2).
options: Admins and mentors; reset replaces the report
Admins only; reset replaces the report
Admins and mentors; try an in-place reset

questions.q: Create the email as a Gmail draft, for Casa Workspace accounts?
questions.context:
What this is about. NW-102. A Google Cloud project under Casa's Workspace, its OAuth consent set to Internal, asks Casa users once for Gmail's compose permission (no Google app review for internal apps). On "Create Gmail draft" the browser gets a short-lived token and puts the Designed email straight into the agent's Drafts, built exactly as it should arrive: no paste problems (left-aligned, italic, blue links). No Gmail tokens stored. Casa Workspace accounts only; personal Gmail keeps Copy. The same Casa Google client also lets Workspace trust the comp report's Google sign-in (Noble's refusal).

Why it needs you. You create the project and client in Casa's Workspace admin (a checklist comes with the dispatch). Build is Phase B.
options: Yes: set up the Casa Google client, build it in Phase B
Not now: Copy stays the only way

questions.q: May the tool store a client's credit or income?
questions.short: Credit and income in the tool
questions.context:
What this is about. You wondered whether agents learn a buyer's credit score, credit-worthiness or income, and whether the tool should hold it. It's noted as a future item, not built.

Why it needs you. It's sensitive financial data about a client who never signed up to the tool, kept in Casa's database. That needs a privacy and legal call (consent, retention, who sees it) before any field exists. A pre-approval already says what a lender thinks the buyer can pay.
options: No: the pre-approval stands in for it; revisit with a privacy review
Yes, as an optional field, after a privacy review
questions.source: Your chat, 2026-10-29 · NW-074 · the client fields PR

questions.q: Where do agents keep their clients today, and can the tool read it?

Why it needs you. Only you know what Casa's agents use. Name it in the note (and whether it has an export or an API); the profiles stay in the roadmap either way.
options: Nowhere the tool can read yet: agents type it into each report
There is one: I'll name it in the note

Built and released: the Designed email and Send (#139, 2026-11-06), then Reports, the shared top bar, Done and a light pass on Sort, the Gate and Findings (the overnight build, 2026-11-06). The questions below are what that build left open. DP-9 and DP-10 are left over from the design port (#77).

questions.q: After Noble: keep Co-op as the default type?
questions.context: Mason's finding in #77: the engine counts like for like, so a co-op report counts no condo comps, and most Tribeca homes are condos. Sort and Findings say so and offer Make this report a condo in one click, which carries the demo. Options for after: default to Condo, or read the type from the home's listing.

questions.q: A full agent's why on the Gate: optional?
questions.context: The handoff makes it optional for graduated (full) agents, and the build does that. New (practice) agents must write 100+ characters.

questions.q: One way to open Hubert: the top-bar pill or the edge tab?
questions.context: What this is about. Hubert opens from a pill in the top bar and from a tab on the screen's edge (#105). Two doors to the same drawer.

questions.q: Sort's compact comp card from the canvas: build it before Nov 13, or after?
questions.context: The canvas's "2 · Sort" opens a comp into a shorter card: your note and actions on one line, the photo beside status, floor, distance and subway, then tags and features as chips. Tonight's build gave Sort the new top bar and header row but kept today's open card, which holds the feature pickers, tags, notes, photos, checks and the per-comp review: the brief said Sort hasn't had its full review with you yet. Rebuilding the card is a day's work and touches the most-used screen just before training.
options: After Nov 13, with its design review
Before Nov 13: design it with me this week, then build

questions.q: The Gate: one number, or a low and a high?
questions.context: The canvas asks for Your number, one figure. The tool asks for a low and a high, and the engine, Findings' bar, Hubert's take and the Access log all use both. Tonight's build kept low and high (now "Your low" and "Your high") and took the canvas's wording: the question names the home, one line under it, and the button reads "Lock it in · Show the range →". One number is a small engine and Findings change, after Nov 13.
options: Keep a low and a high

questions.q: The comp report's new top bar: give the Studio's other tools the same bar?
questions.short: One top bar across the Studio
questions.context: The design pass gave the comp report one bar on every screen: the wordmark, ‹ Studio, the tool's name, the role badge, Hubert, the account and Feedback. The Studio's other tools (the carousel builders, the Property Sign, the profile pics, the CMS) still have their own headers and the floating studio chrome. The brief left them out on purpose (“this is the comp report's bar”). Giving them the same bar is a shared component in assets/ and a pass per tool; nothing about it is needed for Nov 13. Not built: your pick.
options: After Nov 13, one tool at a time

topics.title: The comp report
topics.intro: The comp report is priority one. These come from D-25 and D-17, from the writer's PR (#76) and from Jev's PR (#56).

questions.q: Who reviews the fair-housing list?
questions.context:
What this is about. The writer's QA has one hard block: compliance (D-2). A term on the hard list blocks Copy outright ("adults only", "perfect for young professionals", "no Section 8", "school district", "safe neighborhood"). A word on the near list ("family", "church", "school") warns, and the agent acknowledges it before copying.

Why it needs you. Mason drafted the list from HUD's advertising guidance and New York City's Human Rights Law ({repo}/tools-src/comp-report/workspace/fair-housing.ts, version fh-2026-10-14). A list that blocks agents' emails needs a reviewer before the pilot widens.

questions.q: Does the writer's house voice read right?
questions.context:
What this is about. Claude drafts the headlines and the email's sections in Casa's voice, in Frankie's order. You said to wait for the real eval drafts. They're in: 12 drafts (100 Barclay and Frankie's #517; full, short and text), about $0.20, in project files writer-eval/2026-10-29-eval.md, with the code in #112.

The eval's read. Plain, specific, Frankie's order; 11 of 12 pass every number check. If you want a revision, four fixes: it adds its own points under Things to consider beyond the agent's; one headline gives a single price ("about $4.23M"); the carrying-cost line repeats on every comp; the text message still carries the whole email frame.
options: Fix those four, keep the rest of the voice

questions.q: Jev's seven questions: go with them as written?
questions.context:
What this is about. Jev answers seven fixed questions about each listing's text (sponsor sale, estate sale, tenant in place and the like). The wording is at the end of #56's description. Phase 2 goes live on the reviewed text.

Why it needs you. Casanova read them and found nothing to change. A change after the labelled batch runs means running it again.

questions.q: The ±3 floor band and the ½-mile distance flag most comps. What now?
questions.short: Floor band and distance thresholds: keep?
questions.context:
What this is about. The floor band (±3, from Frankie's email) flags 8 of Hannah's 11 comps; Kara's ½ mile flags 6 of the sample's 11, five of them Primary. A flag is a prompt to the agent, never a block.

Why it needs you. Noble sets or confirms them. Until he does, the numbers stand.
options: Keep them until Noble weighs in
say to what in the note

questions.q: Counsel's two questions: who do they go to, and when?
questions.context:
What this is about. Surveyor found two legal questions research can't settle: (1) is a CMA an "appraisal" under New York law? (2) in sponsor sales, does transfer tax the buyer pays count toward the taxable consideration? Both are in {repo}/docs/comp-report/research/adjustments.md, with sources.

Why it needs you. (1) matters before the pilot; (2) only if the tool ever computes the sponsor arithmetic.
options: Hold until the pilot is near
Send them to a closing attorney now

questions.q: Turn off Netlify Identity's autoconfirm, so password sign-in works?
questions.context:
What this is about. One sign-in for the whole Studio (#116). Password sign-in only works while Identity confirms new accounts by email. While autoconfirm is on, the comp report turns password sign-in off on purpose, because an unconfirmed address proves nothing.

Why it needs you. It's a Netlify setting (Identity, then Emails / Registration). It affects password sign-ups only; Google sign-in is unchanged.
options: new password accounts confirm by email
password sign-in stays off; Google only

questions.q: Require the Studio sign-in on the older functions too?
questions.context:
What this is about. The new Studio sign-in (#116) hides pages but doesn't protect what's behind them. The older functions (Claude copy generation, the StreetEasy import, the image proxy, brand/site) still answer anyone without a signed-in token.

Why it needs you. It's a small follow-up PR, but every tool call would then need a sign-in, including any outside script that calls them (a Make scenario, say). The PR would list every caller it finds first.
options: Yes, in a follow-up PR, after checking what calls them

questions.q: When StreetEasy turns a link read away ("verify you're human"), try once more by itself a minute later?
questions.context: Today the agent has to press Try again. On Nov 6 the same link worked a few minutes later. An automatic retry costs at most one extra Firecrawl read per failure, and the failure still shows if the second try fails too.
options: Yes, one automatic retry about a minute later
No, the agent presses Try again

questions.q: Settings: may agents edit their own profile there (name, phone, photo)?
questions.context: #150 adds Settings (a gear in the name menu). The profile there is read-only for now and still edited in the CMS. Letting agents edit it means writes from Settings into the CMS record, plus a check on photos.

questions.q: Noble's trainees: put them in Practice for the training?
questions.context: From the Friday handoff prep (#154, on top of #143). New sign-ups start as Full, the database default. D-11 says new agents work in Practice until their fifth closing.
options: Noble or you set each trainee to Practice in the Access panel before the session
no build; revisit the default before the wider rollout
New sign-ups default to Practice now
small change; experienced agents then need a grant to Full
Everyone stays on Full for the training

questions.q: The New comp window's step 3: what should it be called?
questions.context: From the New comp port (#168). For now step 3 reads "Own or shared", the canvas's placeholder, which you said you don't love. Renaming it is a single word change. Write the name you want in the note.

questions.q: The home's laundry "None": none listed, or not allowed?
questions.context: From #168. Picking None for the home's laundry saves as "none listed", the same as the old picker did. It could mean "not allowed" in the building instead.

questions.q: Next while the StreetEasy page is being read: wait, or let the agent move on?
questions.context: From #168. Following the canvas, Next stays disabled while the StreetEasy page is read, which usually takes 10 to 40 seconds. Letting the agent move on means the read's results fill in later, behind them.
options: Keep Next disabled until the read finishes
Let the agent move on while it reads
